name: EPAM Systems

Software Engineer (India).dsaDepth: Moderate — a coding assessment (DoSelect/HackerRank), a DSA test, sometimes a group discussion, then 2-3 technical rounds and HR
rounds: Online technical assessment (DoSelect or similar): coding round for initial screening
Nodal/location coding test for some pipelines: DSA questions (e.g. HashMap usage, a parking-lot design problem), with a numeric cutoff (one report: 100/400)
Group discussion round for some campus pipelines (topic example: AI’s effects on UPI), added on the spot for some cohorts
Technical interview(s): resume/project deep-dive, Core Java (OOP, garbage collection, memory allocation), problem-solving, SQL and DSA
Client round(s) for some project-staffed hires: interviews conducted directly with the client team, sometimes including High-Level Design of distributed systems
extraTopics: Core Java internals (garbage collection, memory allocation, OOP pillars) tested in real depth, not just surface-level
Group discussion performance for campus hires — a format not common at most software companies
Being staffed-project-aware: some loops include a "client round" since EPAM is a consultancy assigning engineers to client projects
Software Engineer (India).notes: Round count and sequence vary a lot: reports range from 3 rounds (technical, managerial, HR) to 5 (OA, nodal test, GD, technical, HR) depending on campus vs. off-campus vs. client-specific hiring.
